description: JVM imported classes and cross-module nominal identity slice (ISSUE-0109). JVM-only multi-module fixtures: each fixture writes its 'modules' (relative .deal source paths -> DEAL source) plus 'entry' under a temp project root and runs the real whole-project pipeline -- CompilationOrchestrator with Backend.JVM (module discovery, signature extraction, dependency ordering, name resolution, type checking, per-module JvmBackend codegen) -> javac over every emitted .java artifact plus a runner class -> java executing the emitted artifacts (the harness fails a fixture whose parser/checker/module-discovery yields no compile, whose codegen leaves no artifact, or whose JVM execution is bypassed). Covered forms: exported/imported class declarations (export class emits the same generated nested class as a local one; importers reference the declaring module's generated class Lib.$C_Name), imported-class construction from empty and partial object literals (declared literal defaults applied inline, provided fields reordered to declaration order, provided-field evaluation in literal order across the module boundary), class-typed values passed as parameters and returned across module boundaries (field writes visible through the roundtrip), module-qualified same-name class identity (two modules exporting the same-name same-shape class stay distinct Java types and distinct identity strings), module-qualified runtime nominal checks at the untyped table boundary (success for a genuine instance, E8001 'expected instance of @modela/Item, got @modelb/Item' for a same-name wrong-module instance, E8001 'expected class instance, got null' for a null value), an unused import of a class-exporting module still running its load-time side effects, and one frontend compile-error gate rejected before any backend (E3001 nominal cross-module assignment).

tests.name: jvm-xmod-class-export-import
tests.description: A module exports a class and a factory returning it; the entry annotates the value with the imported qualified type lib.Point, reads its fields, and computes 3 * 10 + 4 = 34 -- the exported class emits the same generated nested class as a local one and the importer references Lib.$C_Point

tests.name: jvm-xmod-class-construction-defaults
tests.description: The entry constructs an imported class directly: the empty literal receives every declared default inline, a partial literal receives defaults for omitted fields, and provided fields land in declaration order regardless of literal order (10 + 20*10 + (2+5) = 217)

tests.name: jvm-xmod-class-construction-eval-order
tests.description: Provided-field evaluation order crosses the module boundary in literal order: mark runs y-first before x-second even though the constructor argument order is x then y, and the sum reads 2 + 5 = 7 (spec sec.Construction provided-fields evaluation)

tests.name: jvm-xmod-class-param-pass
tests.description: A class-typed value passed as a parameter across the module boundary: the entry constructs an imported class and hands it to the declaring module's function, which reads both fields (lib.sum(p) = 12)

tests.name: jvm-xmod-class-return-mutate-roundtrip
tests.description: A class value returned across the module boundary is mutated in the entry and passed back: the write is visible to the declaring module (7 + 5 = 12), pinning reference identity across the boundary

tests.name: jvm-xmod-same-name-isolation
tests.description: Two modules export a same-name same-shape class; the entry binds one instance of each through qualified annotations and calls each module's function -- a:one and b:two prove the Java types (Modela.$C_Item vs Modelb.$C_Item) and the module-qualified identities stay distinct, never conjoined by bare name

tests.name: jvm-xmod-nominal-check-success
tests.description: A genuine instance crossing the slice's untyped boundary (a table field read in an imported-class contextual target) passes the declaring module's runtime nominal check and its field reads back (from-a)

tests.name: jvm-xmod-nominal-check-failure-same-name
tests.description: A same-name instance from a DIFFERENT module fails the imported-class nominal check with E8001 naming both module-qualified identities (expected instance of @src/modelb/Item, got @src/Item) and exit 1 -- identity is module-qualified, never bare-name (runtime-class-identity: the LuaJIT reference conformance pin modid-class-identity fails the same way)

tests.name: jvm-xmod-nominal-check-failure-null
tests.description: A null value crossing an imported-class typed table boundary fails the declaring module's nominal check with E8001 'expected class instance, got null' and exit 1 (the same shape the local-class slice pins for same-module checks)

tests.name: jvm-xmod-class-unused-import-side-effect
tests.description: v1.2 compile-error gate: module top level holds only declarations, so the v1.1 load-time statement in the class-exporting imported module is rejected with E1049 before any backend codegen

modules.main.deal:
import * as lib from "./lib"
export function run(): int { return 1; }

tests.name: jvm-xmod-class-frontend-nominal-error
tests.description: Frontend compile-error gate: assigning a modela.Item value to a modelb.Item annotation is the nominal E3001 type error, rejected before any backend runs (no .java artifacts) -- same-name classes stay nominally distinct at compile time too

tests.name: jvm-xmod-class-param-return-local-fn
tests.description: An entry-local function declares an imported-class parameter and return type: shift(p: lib.Point): lib.Point mutates and returns the value, and the caller reads the returned instance's fields (shifted x=4, sum=8, 8+4=12) — class-typed values pass and return through MAIN-side functions too, not only through the declaring module's
